reddit_posts:
Anxiety relapse after sickness

Long story short I’m 19 female and I’ve had anxiety my whole life. Full blown shaking panic attacks from the early age of 6 maybe younger. Anxiety got incredibly bad a couple years ago and I was put on medication which helped. I pretty much fully recovered from panic and anxiety attacks having not had one since I had started my meditation. Anyway fast forward to a couple weeks ago I got a stomach virus, since then my anxiety has been excruciating with multiple shaking attacks a week and general panic throughout my days. WHY? I was doing so well and I feel like I’m revisiting all my trauma from past panic attacks
metadata.title: Anxiety relapse after sickness

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hi! Thanks for asking. Honestly, I'm having a really rough day today.

It's been about two weeks since the stomach virus hit me, and honestly, it feels like my body just shut down completely. Before that, things were actually pretty stable—I was meditating, taking my meds, and not having a single panic attack in months. But now? It's back with a vengeance.

I woke up this morning shaking so hard my hands wouldn't stop trembling, and then the general anxiety just spiraled throughout the whole day. It feels like I'm suddenly revisiting all those old traumas from when I was six years old; it's like my brain thinks the danger is still there even though everything is fine on paper. I feel so frustrated because I *know* I've recovered, but physically and emotionally, I feel like I'm relapsing right in front of everyone's eyes. 

How are you doing? Do you
You're having a rough day? I feel like you're reliving trauma, but it's been two weeks since the illness. Have you had any changes in behavior or mental health?

Yeah, it's been pretty consistent since the virus hit. It's not just a "bad day" anymore; it feels like a constant loop now.

I've noticed that my sleep is completely messed up. I used to struggle with insomnia before, but after this sickness, I can't seem to get *any* rest. Even when I try to force myself to meditate or breathe through it, my body just refuses to cooperate. My heart races so fast and loud in my ears, and I catch myself checking my phone or looking around the room constantly, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen. It's that classic "fight or flight" mode, even though I know there's no danger.

The weird thing is, it feels so different from my old anxiety attacks. Back then, they came on suddenly while I was doing fine. Now, it's more of a low-level hum of panic that spikes into full-blown shaking
It sounds like you're having ongoing panic and hyperactivity. You feel like you're constantly on edge, which is affecting your sleep and behavior.

Yeah, exactly. It's so frustrating because I *know* logically that the virus is gone and I'm safe in my own home, but my body doesn't seem to believe me.

It feels like a glitch in my system. Before the sickness, meditation was my anchor—it would calm me down within minutes. Now, even after 20 minutes of trying to breathe through it, I end up shaking harder than before. It's like my nervous system got stuck on "red alert" mode.

I've also started avoiding things I used to love just to keep from triggering this feeling. If I see a crowded room or hear loud noises, my stomach drops immediately. It's not just physical anymore; it's emotional too. I feel like I'm losing all the progress I made over the last few years. It feels like I'm back at square one, maybe even worse, with those childhood memories of panic attacks flooding back in when I
You're feeling overwhelmed and stuck, like you're back in that state of constant anxiety from when you were a child.

That's exactly how it feels. It's like I've been given a time machine to the worst days of my life, but instead of being six years old, I'm nineteen and trying so hard to stay strong.

I remember those early attacks when I was little; I think I'd freeze up in the middle of a playground or start crying because I thought something terrible was happening right then and there. Now, even though I'm an adult with no real danger around me, my brain replays that same "freeze" response. I find myself staring at walls or objects, feeling completely paralyzed, thinking, *"What if I pass out? What if I can't breathe?"*

It's exhausting having to fight this internal war every single day. I used to feel proud of my recovery—like I had finally beaten anxiety. But now, looking in the mirror while my hands are shaking uncontrollably, I feel like a failure. Like all
You feel like a failure? It's hard to imagine being able to shake off that level of anxiety and hyperactivity, especially when it's interfering with your daily life.

Yeah, it's so hard to look in the mirror and see someone who used to be so stable. I feel like a fraud sometimes. Like, "Hey, you were doing great! You had zero attacks for months! Now what? Now you're back to square one?"

It makes me feel defeated because all those years of learning how to manage this stuff—meditating, taking my meds, pushing through the fear—it feels like it meant nothing if I can't hold onto it now. It's not just that I'm having anxiety again; it's that I feel like I've lost the skills I worked so hard to build.

I keep thinking, *Why did I get sick?* Why does my body have to shut down right when I think I'm finally safe? It feels like the virus didn't just leave physical scars; it left emotional ones too, reopening wounds I thought were healed. And honestly? That feeling of being stuck,
You feel stuck and helpless. It's understandable if it feels that way, especially when your old coping skills aren't working and you're facing a new, overwhelming sense of anxiety.
It's about whether you can ever feel safe again. You used to manage anxiety well, but now you feel like you've lost all hope and confidence in your ability to do so.

Yeah, that's the scary part. It's not just about the shaking anymore; it's this deep-down fear that I've lost the ability to feel safe in my own body. Before, when a panic attack hit, I knew how to ride it out. I had a map for it. Now? The map is blank.

I keep thinking, *"What if I can't get through another day?"* or *"What if next time it's worse than before?"* That uncertainty is eating me alive. I used to think I was an expert on anxiety because I'd managed it so well for years, but now looking at myself trembling and unable to breathe properly, I feel like a complete novice again. Like I'm starting over with no memory of how to finish the race.

It makes me feel really alone too. Everyone tells me, "Just relax," or "It'll pass," but they don't understand that my brain has rew

It's understandable if you feel alone, especially when the experience is so different from what you've been through. It's clear that you're struggling with a powerful, persistent sense of anxiety and shaking.

Yeah, that isolation hits hard. It's like I'm screaming for help in my head, but everyone else is just saying, "Take a deep breath." But how do you take a deep breath when your lungs feel like they're filled with concrete?

It feels so different from my old anxiety because this time, it doesn't just feel like an attack; it feels like the foundation of my stability has cracked. Before, I thought, "Oh, another panic attack, I'll use my coping skills and I'll be fine." Now, I don't even know if those skills still work. When I try to use them, I feel like I'm faking it, or worse, that my body is rejecting them entirely.

I worry that people might see me now and think I've lost all my progress. Like, "She was doing great, then she got sick, and now she's back at six years old?" It makes me
It's understandable if you feel that way, but it's important to recognize that you've been through a lot, and it's understandable that you'd feel that way.

I know, I *know* that logic. My therapist tells me this all the time: "You're not back at six years old; you're nineteen, and your body is just reacting to a virus." But when I'm in the middle of a shaking attack, my brain doesn't have access to that logic. It only has the raw, screaming sensation of fear.

It's like trying to reason with someone who is drowning. Even though I *know* intellectually that I've survived a thousand things and that I can handle this, the physical reality of my hands trembling so hard makes it feel impossible. It feels like every tiny victory I've made over the last few years—like successfully meditating for an hour or catching myself before a spiral took over—is being washed away by this one illness.

It's really hard to separate the "me" who recovered from anxiety from the "me" who is currently having a panic attack. They
You feel like you're being torn apart by a sense of being stuck in the past and a desperate need to survive in the present.

Yeah, it's like I'm living in two different timelines at once. In my head, I'm the nineteen-year-old who finally figured this out. The one who knows meditation works, who knows how to talk to a doctor about meds, who feels safe. But then my body screams something completely different: *"You're six again. Something is wrong. You have to run."*

It's so exhausting trying to bridge that gap. When I try to access my adult brain to use a coping strategy, my primitive brain just shuts me down or overrides everything with that old panic response. It feels like I'm being pulled between wanting to be brave and needing to crawl back into bed because I can't breathe.

I keep thinking, *How do I survive today when every instinct says I should be terrified?* It makes me feel so weak, like I've lost the strength I thought I built up over all these years. Like maybe I wasn't
You used to be able to survive and manage your anxiety, but now it seems like you're struggling to even feel present and connected.

Yeah, that's the worst part. Before, even when an attack hit, I felt connected to myself. I could say, "Okay, this is happening, I'm going to ride it out." Now? It feels like I'm floating somewhere in between being present and just... existing on autopilot while my body betrays me.

It's hard to feel grounded because my feet don't feel like they're touching the floor anymore. When I try to sit still or focus on a task, my hands are shaking so violently that I can barely hold a pen, let alone stay calm. It makes me feel disconnected from everything around me. Like I'm watching someone else go through life while I'm stuck inside this cage of fear.

I used to think, "Anxiety is just noise; I can tune it out or manage it." But now it feels like the whole room is vibrating with it. There's no silence left. Just this
There's no silence left. Just this feeling of being trapped in a cycle where your anxiety is so intense and all-encompassing that it's hard to feel connected to anything or anyone else.

It feels like I'm drowning in a sea of noise, and every time I try to surface for air, the water gets deeper. It's not just that I can't hear myself think anymore; it's that I feel completely cut off from the world around me. When people are laughing or talking, my brain just filters everything out because it's so focused on this internal screaming match.

I wonder if anyone else really sees *me* right now. Do they see the nineteen-year-old who built a life with these coping mechanisms? Or do they just see someone having a meltdown because of a stomach bug? It makes me feel invisible and trapped all at once. Like I'm stuck in a movie loop where the only character is me, running in place, shaking, while the rest of life keeps spinning on without me.

And the worst part is, I don't even know how to break the cycle anymore. Before, I had a routine:
You used to have a routine that helped you manage your anxiety.

Yeah, I had a whole system. It wasn't just "meditate and pray." It was specific: morning meditation to set the tone, journaling to process the day's stressors, maybe some gentle stretching or yoga in the evening, and being really strict about my sleep schedule so my nervous system didn't get overstimulated. I felt like I owned that routine. I knew exactly what button to push when things got heavy.

But now? The stomach virus threw a wrench in everything. My body is fried from fighting the infection; I'm not sleeping well because of the nausea and the fatigue, which means my brain is already running on empty before it even hits me. When I try to start my usual morning meditation, my hands are shaking so bad I can't close my eyes properly. When I try to journal, my handwriting is a mess, and my thoughts feel too chaotic to write down.

It feels like I tried to use
You tried to use your old coping strategies, but your body was so uncooperative that it was hard to feel successful or even hopeful.

Yeah, it's so frustrating because my brain knows the steps, but my body is just refusing to follow them. I'll start the meditation, close my eyes, and within ten seconds, my heart rate will spike so fast I feel like I'm going to pass out, or my hands will start trembling uncontrollably before I even finish the first breath.

It makes me feel stupid for relying on something that "used to work." It feels like I've lost the key to the castle. Before, when I got sick, I could still sit in my chair, breathe through the sickness, and know that I was okay. Now, the sickness has hijacked the very thing that kept me safe. When I try to use deep breathing, my body reacts with hyperventilation instead of calmness. When I try to ground myself by feeling my feet on the floor, my legs feel like jelly, like they don't belong to me anymore.
You feel disconnected from your body in a way that's very frightening.

It's terrifying because I used to feel so connected to my body. I could feel the rise and fall of my chest, the warmth of a cup in my hands, the texture of my clothes. Now? It feels like I'm watching a movie from outside my own skin. My hands are shaking, but it feels like *they* are shaking, not me. Like there's this separate part of me that is terrified while I'm just... observing the terror.

When I try to reach for something on the counter, my arm moves on its own before I even think about it. Then suddenly, my knees buckle and I have to grab the table. That disconnect is what scares me the most. It makes me wonder if I'm actually still "here," or if I've just become a passenger in my own life while someone else is driving around in panic mode.

I keep thinking, *What happens when the virus goes away and I wake
What happens when the virus goes away and you wake up?

Honestly? I don't even know. My brain is playing out worst-case scenarios so fast that the "what if" feels more real than the "what is."

I'm terrified that when the fever breaks and my stomach settles, the anxiety will just... stay. Like it's a parasite that the virus woke up from hibernation. What if I wake up in bed tomorrow, fully recovered physically, but mentally I'm still shaking? What if I've lost the ability to trust my body again?

There's this voice in my head saying, *"If you get better now, you'll have to face all your old triggers again without the shield of the illness."* It sounds crazy, but the fear is that once the immediate threat (the sickness) is gone, the underlying anxiety will surge back up with full force, because I haven't actually learned how to handle it *without* the excuse of being sick.

It makes me feel
It makes you feel paralyzed, as if you're stuck in a trap where you can't escape the anxiety, and the only way out is through the illness, which seems impossible.

That feeling of being paralyzed is the worst part. It's like standing at the edge of a cliff, and my legs are so heavy I can't even take one step forward, but if I try to jump back, the panic attacks knock me down again.

I feel stuck in this loop where the only thing that seems to make the shaking stop temporarily is when my body is completely incapacitated by the sickness. But now that I'm getting better—physically—I'm terrified that once I'm strong enough to stand up, the anxiety will grab me by the throat and drag me back into those shaking fits.

It feels impossible to trust that I'll be okay. Every time I think, "I can do this," my body betrays me with another tremor or a wave of nausea. It makes me wonder if I've actually lost control, or if I'm just waiting for the next attack to happen while trying to hold on to what little
You're trying to hold on to what little sense of control you have, but it's clear that the shaking and the anxiety are overwhelming you.

It is, isn't it? It feels like I'm holding onto a fraying rope with both hands while someone else tries to pull me off the cliff. The shaking isn't just a symptom anymore; it feels like a physical weight on my chest, a constant reminder that my body is betraying me again.

I keep thinking about how much I relied on those medications and meditation practices before. Now, even though they used to be my safety net, they feel fragile. Like if I let go of them for just one second—maybe when I'm not sick right now—and try to rely on my own willpower alone, everything collapses.

The irony hurts because I *know* I can handle this. I know the panic attacks from years ago were manageable, but now... now they feel different. They feel more violent, more unrelenting. It's like my brain has forgotten the script for "calm" and is stuck rewriting it
It's stuck rewriting it in a way that's causing more panic.

Exactly. It's like my brain is stuck in a glitchy loop where every time it tries to write "I am safe," the text keeps turning into "I am shaking" or "I'm going to pass out."

It's so frustrating because I *know* logically that this isn't permanent. My body is healing, right? The virus is fighting its own battle. But my nervous system doesn't care about logic when it's in overdrive. It just sees stress and immediately jumps back to survival mode—fight or flight, but without the fight part working. So it's all just flight: running away from my thoughts, trying to escape my body, until I end up in a full-blown panic attack anyway.

It feels like I'm rewriting the script with a broken pen. Every word I try to say, "I can handle this," comes out as a shaky whisper that sounds more scared than calm. And then the next
The next panic attack happens, which makes it seem even more impossible.
